description.value: The Port Alice Branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library has served this remote North Vancouver Island community since 1972, on the unceded traditional territory of the Quatsino nation. As one of the few public indoor spaces in Port Alice, it offers free WiFi, public computers, printing, and photocopying in a wheelchair-accessible building. For touring cyclists riding the isolated north island routes, it provides a rare opportunity to rest indoors and get connected.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website's Branch Features section explicitly lists 'Free public WiFi', confirming the OSM internet_access=wlan/fee=no tags. No mention of bike parking, washrooms, water refill, or any cycling-specific amenities anywhere in the website content or OSM tags. The website content was truncated before the full contact information section rendered, so phone and address could not be cross-checked against the website.
concerns: Website content was truncated before the Contact Information section rendered, preventing verification of phone number and street address against OSM data.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A public library in a small, remote community is a genuinely useful waypoint for touring cyclists on the north island; free WiFi and public computers are confirmed amenities of direct value to cyclists passing through Port Alice.

wow_evidence: Library ladder 1/1. One of few indoor public spaces in Port Alice; scarcity uplift stays downstream.
blurb: Public library since 1972; WiFi, computers, one of few indoor stops in Port Alice.
